nodes.What it is: The basic rules of electricity a robot runs on: voltage, current, resistance (Ohm's law), power, and how to read a schematic. You use a multimeter and breadboard to check that a circuit does what you think before you plug in a motor.
nodes._accessibility_reason: Cheap kit, huge amount of beginner tutorials, results in days.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Stable knowledge; free browser circuit simulators (Falstad, Wokwi) let students learn before buying parts.
nodes.Key players: Arduino, SparkFun, Adafruit (education); Texas Instruments app notes
nodes.Best resources: Arduino Learn hub; SparkFun & Adafruit tutorials; Falstad circuit simulator

nodes.What it is: A microcontroller (MCU) is a tiny computer on one chip that reads sensors and drives motors with precise timing. Firmware is the C/C++ (or Rust/MicroPython) program flashed onto it; it runs without a full operating system.
nodes.Prerequisites: C programming; Electronics fundamentals for robots.
nodes._accessibility_reason: Software-strong team: firmware is just code with timers and pins; boards cost €5-40.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Mainstream boards: ESP32-S3 (dual-core 240 MHz, Wi-Fi/BLE, vector instructions for NN), Raspberry Pi Pico 2 (RP2350), Teensy 4.1 (Cortex-M7 600 MHz), STM32 family. Arduino UNO Q pairs a Linux MPU with an STM32U585 MCU on one board. Embedded Rust (Embassy) is growing.
nodes.Key players: Espressif, Raspberry Pi, STMicroelectronics, PJRC, Arduino, Rust Embedded WG
nodes.Best resources: Cornell ECE 4760 (RP2350, free lectures); PlatformIO; The Embedded Rust Book
nodes.Sources: https://www.espressif.com/en/products/socs/esp32-s3 ; https://datasheets.raspberrypi.com/pico/pico-2-product-brief.pdf ; https://www.pjrc.com/store/teensy41.html ; https://docs.arduino.cc/hardware/uno-q/ ; https://ece4760.github.io/ ; https://platformio.org/ ; https://docs.rust-embedded.org/book/ ; https://embassy.dev/

nodes.What it is: Buses are the 'languages' chips and boards use to talk: UART (simple serial), I2C and SPI (sensors on one board), and CAN / CAN FD (robust, multi-node bus used in cars and in most robot joints). Choosing and debugging the right bus is daily work in robotics.
nodes._accessibility_reason: Concepts are software-like (protocols, packets); need a logic analyzer and care with wiring.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: CAN FD is the de-facto bus for low-cost quadruped/humanoid actuators (moteus, ODrive, CubeMars, RobStride); CAN XL is the newest generation standardised by CiA. ESP32 has a built-in CAN controller (TWAI).
nodes.Key players: CAN in Automation (CiA), Bosch, Espressif, SparkFun
nodes.Best resources: SparkFun I2C tutorial; CiA CAN knowledge pages; ESP-IDF TWAI docs

nodes.What it is: Smart servos (Feetech STS, Robotis Dynamixel) are motor + gearbox + controller in one box, chained on a single serial bus and commanded with position targets. They are how most low-cost robot arms such as the SO-101 are built.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: The SO-101 arm (6x STS3215, 1/345 gear) is the reference low-cost platform for imitation learning via LeRobot; Dynamixel Protocol 2.0 remains the research standard.
nodes.Key players: Feetech, ROBOTIS, The Robot Studio, Hugging Face
nodes.Best resources: LeRobot SO-101 docs; Dynamixel Protocol 2.0 e-manual

nodes.What it is: A microcontroller pin can't power a motor; a motor driver (H-bridge, MOSFET stage) switches the battery current on and off very fast (PWM) to control speed and torque. This node covers brushed DC, stepper and the basics of brushless (BLDC) drivers, current sensing and heat.
nodes.Prerequisites: Electronics fundamentals for robots; Microcontrollers & bare-metal firmware.
nodes._accessibility_reason: Off-the-shelf driver boards are easy; understanding and debugging power stages takes real electrical skill and can burn parts.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Integrated driver ICs (e.g. TI DRV88xx) cover small robots; high-power robot joints use dedicated BLDC controllers.
nodes.Key players: Texas Instruments, Infineon, STMicroelectronics, ODrive Robotics
nodes.Best resources: TI DRV8833 datasheet and TI motor-driver app notes

nodes.What it is: Brushless motors power almost every modern legged robot and drone. Field-oriented control (FOC) is the algorithm that turns encoder angle and phase currents into smooth, precise torque. Open boards (ODrive, moteus, SimpleFOC) let you use it without designing the power stage.
nodes.Prerequisites: Motor drivers & power electronics; basic control (PID).
nodes._accessibility_reason: Open-source boards and libraries exist, but tuning and safety need care; actuator cost €50-300 each.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Quasi-direct-drive actuators popularised by MIT Mini Cheetah (Katz, 2018) are the norm; open controllers (ODrive S1/Pro, mjbots moteus, SimpleFOC v2.4) and Chinese integrated actuators (CubeMars, RobStride) dropped prices sharply.
nodes.Key players: ODrive Robotics, mjbots, SimpleFOC community, CubeMars, RobStride, MIT Biomimetic Robotics Lab
nodes.Best resources: SimpleFOC docs; moteus reference manual; Katz MIT thesis 'A low cost modular actuator for dynamic robots'
nodes.Sources: https://simplefoc.com/ ; https://github.com/simplefoc/Arduino-FOC ; https://odriverobotics.com/ ; https://github.com/odriverobotics/ODrive ; https://github.com/mjbots/moteus ; https://github.com/mjbots/moteus/blob/main/docs/reference.md ; https://dspace.mit.edu/handle/1721.1/118671 ; https://www.cubemars.com/ ; https://robstride.com/

nodes.What it is: Robots read the world through encoders, IMUs, current and force sensors. This node is the electrical side: ADCs, pull-ups, filtering noise, sampling rates and timestamps, so the data your AI model gets is clean.
nodes.Prerequisites: Microcontrollers & bare-metal firmware; Communication buses (UART, I2C, SPI, CAN).
nodes._accessibility_reason: Mostly code and breakout boards; noise debugging needs an oscilloscope.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Unknown specific 2026 shift; trend is more sensors per joint (magnetic encoders on-board controllers, e.g. ODrive S1).
nodes.Key players: Bosch Sensortec, TDK InvenSense, Adafruit, SparkFun (unverified as a list; see Sensing branch)
nodes.Best resources: SparkFun & Adafruit tutorials; Cornell ECE 4760 labs

nodes.What it is: How a robot gets its energy: lithium battery packs, battery management systems (BMS), voltage regulators, fuses and wiring that can carry the current. Bad power design is the #1 cause of resets, fires and dead boards.
nodes._accessibility_reason: Concepts are simple, but LiPo safety must be learned and respected.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Unknown for this node beyond general practice; reference guidance on Li-ion care from Battery University.

nodes.What it is: Bigger robots pair the microcontroller with a small Linux computer (Raspberry Pi, Jetson, Arduino UNO Q) that runs cameras, ROS 2 and AI models, while the MCU handles hard real-time motor loops. Knowing how to split work between them is a key design skill.
nodes._accessibility_reason: Pure software territory for this team; boards €60-250.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Hybrid MPU+MCU boards are mainstream (Arduino UNO Q: Qualcomm QRB2210 Debian + STM32U585 on Zephyr). Raspberry Pi AI HAT+ adds a Hailo accelerator.
nodes.Best resources: Arduino UNO Q docs; Raspberry Pi AI HAT+ product info; NVIDIA Jetson docs

nodes.What it is: Motor and balance controllers must run on time, every time (e.g. every 1 ms). A real-time OS (FreeRTOS, Zephyr) or real-time Linux (PREEMPT_RT) schedules tasks so deadlines are never missed. This is where many software engineers first meet 'jitter'.
nodes.Prerequisites: Microcontrollers & bare-metal firmware; OS concepts (threads, interrupts).
nodes._accessibility_reason: OS concepts are familiar to 42 students; measuring timing needs a scope/logic analyzer.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: PREEMPT_RT was merged into mainline Linux 6.12 (Nov 2024) after ~20 years; Zephyr is used by Arduino UNO Q for its MCU side.
nodes.Key players: FreeRTOS (AWS), Zephyr Project (Linux Foundation), Linux kernel RT maintainers
nodes.Best resources: Lee & Seshia 'Introduction to Embedded Systems' (free, Berkeley EECS149); FreeRTOS and Zephyr docs

nodes.What it is: The software glue between your electronics and ROS 2: ros2_control defines hardware interfaces and controllers, and micro-ROS runs a ROS 2 node directly on a microcontroller (e.g. ESP32). Done well, the same code drives the simulated and the real robot.
nodes.Prerequisites: Embedded Linux & companion computers; ROS 2 basics.
nodes._accessibility_reason: Software-heavy; documentation is decent but integration debugging takes time.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: ros2_control docs ship an 'Embedded Integration' section (2026); micro-ROS moved its site to micro.vulcanexus.org and supports ESP-IDF.

nodes.What it is: EtherCAT is a real-time Ethernet used by industrial arms and high-end humanoids to synchronise dozens of motor drives at kHz rates. Open-source masters (SOEM) make it usable from a Linux PC.
nodes.Prerequisites: Communication buses (UART, I2C, SPI, CAN); Real-time OS & real-time control loops.
nodes._accessibility_reason: Drives and slaves are expensive and the stack is complex; low priority for a 4-6 month student lab.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: IEC-standardised, originated at Beckhoff; dominant in industrial robotics.
nodes.Key players: Beckhoff, EtherCAT Technology Group, Open EtherCAT Society

nodes.What it is: Designing your own printed circuit board replaces a fragile nest of jumper wires with a clean, reliable board: schematic capture, layout, ordering from a fab. KiCad is the free, professional-grade tool.
nodes.Prerequisites: Electronics fundamentals for robots; Sensor interfacing & signal conditioning.
nodes._accessibility_reason: Tool is free and fabs are cheap, but each board iteration takes 1-2 weeks and first boards often have bugs.

nodes.What it is: Running neural networks on the robot itself instead of the cloud: from tiny models on microcontrollers (TinyML) to vision accelerators (Hailo) to GPU modules (Jetson) that can run VLAs. Choosing the chip sets your latency, power and battery life.
nodes.Prerequisites: Embedded Linux & companion computers; deep learning basics.
nodes._accessibility_reason: Team's AI strength applies directly; Jetson Orin Nano Super is affordable, Thor is €3.5k+.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Jetson AGX Thor (Blackwell, up to 2070 FP4 TFLOPS, 128 GB, 40-130 W; dev kit $3,499, Aug 2025) targets on-board humanoid VLAs; Jetson Orin Nano Super gives 67 TOPS; Hailo-8 26 TOPS; LiteRT for Microcontrollers and Edge Impulse cover MCU-scale models.
nodes.Key players: NVIDIA, Hailo, Google (LiteRT), Edge Impulse, Espressif
nodes.Best resources: NVIDIA Jetson pages; LiteRT for Microcontrollers guide; Edge Impulse docs

nodes.What it is: Testing firmware before (or without) real hardware: browser simulators (Wokwi), full-system emulators (Renode) and hardware-in-the-loop rigs where the real board talks to a simulated robot. Saves burned parts and enables CI for firmware.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Renode (Antmicro) emulates multi-node systems; Wokwi simulates ESP32/RP2040/Arduino in the browser.

nodes.Node: Electrical safety & functional safety for robots
nodes.What it is: How to make sure a robot fails safe: emergency stops that really cut motor power, current limits, watchdogs, and the standards (ISO 13849 for safety-related control systems) industry uses. Mandatory before any public demo.
nodes.Prerequisites: Motor drivers & power electronics; Batteries & power distribution.
nodes._accessibility_reason: E-stop and watchdog basics are easy; formal functional safety is a specialist field.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: ISO 13849-1 is in its 4th edition (2023); ISO pages blocked our fetch so details beyond Wikipedia are unverified.

nodes.Node: Open-source actuator & electronics stacks for legged/humanoid robots
nodes.What it is: Whole open designs that combine BLDC actuators, CAN buses and on-board compute into a walking robot, e.g. Berkeley Humanoid Lite (< $5,000, 3D-printed gearboxes) or Open Duck Mini. They show how the electronics of a full robot fit together.
nodes.Prerequisites: BLDC motor control & field-oriented control (FOC); Communication buses (UART, I2C, SPI, CAN); Batteries & power distribution.
nodes._accessibility_reason: Integrating 10-20 actuators, power and compute is a multi-month effort even with open designs.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Berkeley Humanoid Lite (2025, arXiv 2504.17249) and Open Duck Mini v2 (~42 cm Disney BDX-like) are reproducible open platforms; MIT Mini Cheetah lineage underpins actuator designs.
nodes.Key players: UC Berkeley (Hybrid Robotics), Open Duck Mini community, MIT Biomimetic Robotics Lab, mjbots
nodes.Best resources: Berkeley Humanoid Lite site/paper; Open Duck Mini repo
